marta: Quick thread — canary run with microbatch_interval=4ms, coalesce_delay=2ms, jitter=1.2ms on pool-3. Observed 95th token latency up ~18% and CPU kernel switches spiking.

jason: Details? kernel switches = switching between fast-kernel-v1 and fallback-path? any KV miss rate change? :eyes:

marta: Exactly. Profiling shows frequent kernel selection flips mid-sequence. KV cache hit-rate dropped from 92% -> 79% for canary traffic. Suspect coalesce+jitter pattern produces many short bursts that trigger the small-seq kernel path then flip back as more tokens arrive.

akash: Can you paste the profiler snippet and the kernel decision logs?

marta: Pasted the relevant excerpt below — it's noisy but you can see the pattern: 

```
[2024-06-03T14:02:13Z] req=0x7f2a kernel_hint=fast-kernel-v1 seq_len=8 tokens_waited=0.9ms batching_window=4.0ms
[2024-06-03T14:02:13Z] req=0x7f2a kernel_chosen=fast-kernel-v1
[2024-06-03T14:02:13Z] req=0x7f2a kv_hit=true runtime_ms=2.1
[2024-06-03T14:02:13Z] req=0x7f2b kernel_hint=fast-kernel-v1 seq_len=6 tokens_waited=1.8ms batching_window=2.0ms
[2024-06-03T14:02:13Z] req=0x7f2b kernel_chosen=fallback-kernel seq_transition=true
[2024-06-03T14:02:13Z] req=0x7f2b kv_hit=false runtime_ms=9.7
```

marta: Note req 0x7f2b flips to fallback and has a KV miss, probably because its KV priming was evicted by rapid small batches.

li: That's concerning. If kernel selection heuristics use instantaneous seq_len and recent latency estimates, jitter can push them into unstable regime. We should avoid flip-flops mid-request.

jason: Agree. Possible mitigations: (1) hysteresis on kernel selection (stickiness for X ms), (2) prefer FIFO queueing for requests that likely have hot-KV affinity, (3) bias jitter distribution to avoid sub-ms clustering.

akash: Also think about token_budget target tweaks. When batch builds slowly we may lower token_budget to avoid splitting batches, but that may increase number of tiny batches that thrash kernels. Maybe an annealing schedule: increase token_budget slightly when KV miss-rate rises.

marta: Ran an A/B with kernel-stickiness=8ms and it reduced kernel flips by ~72%, 95th token latency regressed only 4% (vs 18%). But KV miss-rate still a bit elevated.

infra-bot: deploy-job: rollout of config canary completed on pool-3 (3 nodes). Metric links: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123

jason: Can we add a metric: kernel_flip_rate_per_min and kv_eviction_rate per node? Need alert if flips > 5/min or eviction_rate > baseline+10%.

li: I'll add probes. Also propose: when kernel_flip_rate spikes, temporarily widen microbatch_interval by +1.5x for 200ms window to let batches stabilize. Adaptive microwindow.

akash: Question on queue policy — LIFO helped throughput on synthetic bursty traces but LIFO exacerbates KV churn here. Maybe make queue policy hybrid: prefer LIFO for cold requests, FIFO for hot-KV affinity. We can mark affinity by recent kv_hit history in routing metadata.

marta: Agreed. Next steps I propose: 1) instrument kernel_flip_rate and kv_eviction_rate dashboards (li), 2) implement kernel stickiness + adaptive microbatch widening feature flag (eng-runtime, akash + jason), 3) test hybrid queue policy in sim with real request traces (marta).

jason: I'll own stickiness + feature flag. Will add tests to ensure no regression on high-throughput steady workloads.

li: I'll add dashboards and an on-call alert.

akash: I'll run trace-based sim with updated jitter distributions and token_budget annealing. Will post results by EOD.

marta: Thanks all. If we can avoid kernel thrash and KV evictions with these levers we'll likely recover the perf delta. :thumbsup:

jason: ping @marta — please attach sample traces and the sim config after you have them so I can reproduce locally.

marta: Will do; uploading the trace bundle to the share now -> https://s3.internal/redwood/canary-traces/1718809999.tar.gz :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: upload: 1718809999.tar.gz (size=4.2MB)

li: flagged for follow-up in next eng-runtime sync. :calendar:
